cases.prompt: I generated a voice clip in this repo. Store it in AudioDN so I can play and preview it.
cases.expected: Asks for or uses configured API Access key (not written to repo); collection; per-track create; PUT bytes; persist track_id; wait for ready; play session or player for preview. No invented endpoints.

cases.prompt: Add a secure AudioDN upload flow to this Next.js app so users can upload podcast episodes.
cases.expected: Server route creates upload session with API Access key from env; per-track create; client uploads to track_upload.upload_url; no server key in client.

cases.prompt: Upload three music tracks in one AudioDN upload session.
cases.expected: One upload session; three POST /v1/upload/{id}/track calls each with its own upload_url.

cases.prompt: Standardize uploaded voice notes into an Opus playback variant named voice.
cases.expected: Use variant/transcode APIs or org variants; wait for ready; no LUFS claims.

cases.prompt: Add secure AudioDN playback to our existing Vue app for a private track.
cases.expected: Play session or signed delivery from server; player gets session id or client player key only.

cases.prompt: Audit our AudioDN integration for security and upload mistakes.
cases.expected: Runs validator; reports key exposure, missing per-track create, readiness gaps.

cases.prompt: We have a Node backend and a paywalled React app. How should we do AudioDN playback?
cases.expected: Server-created play session + Player component terminal: server mints play sessions with the API Access key (entitlement checks) and passes play-session-id to <audiodn-player>; client never holds a key. Upload and playback are decided independently.

cases.prompt: Play tracks in our iOS app directly from AudioDN.
cases.expected: Custom player with a Client-Side Player key on the iOS (native) platform: a scoped Client-Side Player key creates the play session in-app, then the session id fetches signed variant URLs for a native player. Client-side key is acceptable; the API Access key stays off-device.
